thread:
irene: Draft: 'staged activation' flow for air-gapped packaging. idea: split upgrade into immutable base + ordered micro-layers. each micro-layer has digest, chunk-index (for resume), signer metadata, and a small rollout policy. goal: fast verification, resumable transport, clear commit semantics.

mike: nice. how are layers ordered and how do we avoid two operators applying different orders?

irene: ordering is explicit: activation-list is an ordered array of layer descriptors with sequence numbers. the activation-list itself is signed and content-addressed. operators persist applied-seq in a local store (boltdb) and never advance past a signed activation-list reference.

sasha: what about partial apply semantics? if a node finishes layer 5 then fails on 6, admin needs to know whether 5 is safe-to-announce.

irene: two markers: durable_seq (announced) and inprogress_seq (applied but uncommitted). durable_seq only advances after the configured commit-phase completes. inprogress is transient and cleared on retry or commit.

ops_kim: commit-phase meaning? cluster consensus?

irene: two modes. single-node mode: operator commits locally after successful apply and verification. quorum-mode: operator exchanges commit-tokens with peer-specified nodes and only moves durable_seq forward when quorum of tokens are received. tokens are short-lived signed receipts to avoid replay.

mike: tokens seem useful. how do we prevent token replay if someone copies them?

irene: token contains activation-list hash, seq, node-id, expiry, and operator signature. operators reject tokens with expired timestamps or mismatched activation-list hash. we recommend rekeying operator signing keys periodically.

sasha: offline transfer: how should admins build bundles for physical media?
irene: produce a 'bundle' directory: activation-list.json (signed), blobs/ (content-addressed chunk files), prefetch-index.txt (one hash per line), and optional signatures/{layer}.sig. pack to tar.gz. operator verify command reads activation-list and ensures blobs present, validating chunk checksums.

pkg-bot: note: adding CLI subcommands for bundle inspect/verify/plan/apply. noted in backlog.

ops_kim: resume: if a blob transfer is interrupted, does operator re-request whole blob or chunk-diff?

irene: we use fixed-size chunks addressed by sha256. transfers can resume per chunk. bundle format includes chunk-map metadata so operator can skip already-present chunks. remote transfer agents (scp/usb) just copy files; transfer resume mainly matters for remote http gateway used during pre-staging.

mike: migration: customers on 'monolithic delta' format will need a converter. plan?

irene: write a conversion tool that slices monolithic delta into chunked blobs and emits activation-list with seq mapping. operator accepts both old 'delta.json' and new 'activation-list' formats for ~6 months. add warning logs when loading legacy bundles.

sasha: security: some customers require signer per-release AND signer per-operator (two signatures). support policy?

irene: yes - support layered signing: publisher signs each layer; operator/ops team signs activation-list. operator validates both against a local trust store which can be cluster-level or per-node. we also support HSM-backed verification via PKCS#11 plugins.

ops_kim: what about replay protection when a bundle is used on a rebuilt machine?

irene: activation-list includes a short activation_window and optional nonce bound to an installation-id. default behavior: if installation-id present in manifest and mismatch, operator rejects activation. for consumer installs we leave install-id absent but rely on TTL windows to reduce replay risk.

mike: observability: what metrics/traces should we add?

sasha: propose metrics: operator_activation_inprogress_seq, operator_activation_durable_seq, operator_layer_apply_duration_seconds{layer}, operator_commit_ack_count, operator_last_sync_error. logs: structured audit lines for stage/commit/rollback with activation-list hash and seq.

irene: agree. also include a remediation plan: 'redwoodctl activation repair --target <node>' that prints minimal blob set and commands to nudge node to converge.

pkg-bot: backlog task created: activation repair CLI + explainers. ticket #PKG-784.

ops_kim: runbook for stuck commit? ops checklist would be handy.

irene: runbook snippet to include in RFC: 1) run redwoodctl activation status --verbose 2) collect operator logs: /var/log/redwood/operator.log 3) if in quorum-mode check peer ACKs: redwoodctl peers list --show-acks 4) to abort staged activation: redwoodctl activation abort --seq <n> (requires operator-auth) 5) to force-commit (emergency): redwoodctl activation force-commit --seq <n> --manual-override (audit required).

mike: force-commit should emit an audit event and require an allowlist of identities. good.

sasha: policies: we need to allow per-customer policy profiles: e.g., "safe-default" (quorum required), "fast-default" (single-node), "manual-gate" (requires human approval). store profile in operator config.

irene: yep. operator config prototype: {"activation_policy":"safe-default","trusted_signers":[...],"quorum_members":[...],"commit_timeout_secs":600}. we'll include schema in RFC.

ops_kim: test plan?

irene: tests: unit for state transitions; integration cluster tests with 3 nodes in quorum-mode; chaos test where we kill operator mid-chunk-transfer; end-to-end on-device verify/apply using USB bundles.

sasha: add a performance benchmark for bundle verify time on low-end disks. admins will ask.

irene: noted. I'll add benchmark targets and acceptable thresholds.

audit-bot: policy-note: activation TTL enforcement enabled by default for enterprise accounts.

mike: I'll review the RFC draft later today. thanks irene.

irene: thanks all 5 leaving this thread open for comments for 10 days before merging the RFC into docs/rfcs.
